svg.title: Architecture of the Looker agent on Agent Substrate
svg.desc: A business user reaches Looker over HTTPS. Looker's server calls the agent gateway with a chat credential. The gateway calls the Substrate ingress router over mutual TLS, which reaches the agent in a gVisor sandbox. The agent can only reach the Looker API and the model endpoint, both through the Substrate egress gateway, which adds the model credential.
svg.text: Customer-hosted Looker, the agent in a sandbox, and the only paths in and out. Kubernetes you operate: on-prem or GKE.
The chat is a Looker extension
in a sandboxed frame. It holds
Web UI and API over HTTPS. Its server makes the chat's calls to the gateway
and adds the chat credential from a hidden user attribute.
Non-root, no privilege escalation, no capabilities, no cluster token.
Its API port accepts the Substrate egress gateway only.
Authenticates every caller, and will not start
without credentials. The chat credential may
send only the chat's exact requests. Limits on
Allowlist by host name: other names do not
Swaps the placeholder for the model credential.
Renders dashboards as images, answers data questions, returns links.
Holds the Looker API key of one least-privilege Looker user, and a
placeholder where the model credential belongs.
May query only the LookML models it is configured for.
Queried by Looker with the connections
Vertex AI only. On GKE: Workload Identity.
The agent image is pulled by digest.
Snapshots of the agent, which include
the Looker API key, go to an object
Looker's server adds the chat credential.
Mutual TLS. The gateway, not the caller, names the agent.
Only identities on the router's allowlist get this far.
One Looker identity for every user.
The real credential is added here.
Default deny in the kit's namespaces; only these paths are open.
Non-root, no privilege escalation, capabilities dropped.
Generated at install. Never on a command line or in Terraform state.
Substrate pinned to a commit, the agent image to a digest.
KNOW BEFORE YOU RELY ON IT
The agent answers with one Looker identity:
every chat user sees what that identity can see.
Worker pods are privileged. The sandbox, not the
pod, is what contains the agent.
